title: Hackers Are Turning Up the Heat

source.headline: High-profile tech outages show how vulnerable our tech is — even fridges
source.author: Jenna McLaughlin

article: As the holiday season got under way in the United States, a {1|spate} of high-profile tech outages briefly knocked out email and disrupted flight communications. Officials say the breakdowns were not a coordinated attack, and even a simple software {2|glitch} can cause chaos at the busiest time of year. Still, the episode has revived an uncomfortable question: how easily could someone break the machines that quietly keep everyday life running?

One worrying answer comes from an unlikely place: the freezer. In late August, freezers at the commissary of Fort Irwin, a U.S. Army base in California, began overheating, and at least five other bases reported the same problem. The Pentagon has declined to share details of its investigation, but most experts suspect a cyberattack. In France, refrigeration systems in 500 to 700 supermarkets failed overnight, spoiling millions of euros’ worth of food. Similar incidents followed in early November in Estonia, Sweden and the Netherlands. French officials blamed hackers linked to Iran’s military; Tehran denies involvement, and no individual {3|perpetrator} has been publicly named.

These systems belong to what engineers call operational technology, or OT — the hardware that controls physical processes such as cooling and pumping. Earlier this year, Iranian hackers also disrupted water treatment facilities across the U.S. Security researchers say many such devices sit on the open internet with {4|lax} protection: known flaws left unpatched and basic safeguards missing. One researcher called internet-exposed devices the “soft belly” of security. In an earlier case at an Israeli food company, attackers who {5|tampered with} freezer controls destroyed the compressors while office printers spat out propaganda. A responder believes AI let them test settings far faster than any human could.

Experts warn that the next {6|brazen} attack could wreak {7|havoc} on far more than frozen peas. Vaccines, blood banks, ports and power plants all depend on similar equipment. Industry groups are urging Washington to set basic security requirements so that private operators {8|shore up} their defenses before a bad actor succeeds. Many argue that privately owned critical infrastructure now needs real regulation. For families at Fort Irwin, the lesson is already clear: be prepared for anything.
summary_zh: 感恩節前美國接連發生大型科技服務中斷，再度引發「日常基礎設施有多脆弱」的討論。從美軍基地到法國等歐洲國家的超市，冷凍設備接連被駭、溫度失控；法國指向與伊朗軍方有關的駭客，伊朗否認。專家指出，大量「營運技術（OT）」設備直接暴露在網路上、防護鬆散，AI 又讓攻擊更快，因此呼籲政府訂定基本資安要求。
